A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KinDEL study and retain identifiable experiments on the same molecular library. Their text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original MAPK14 and DDR1 screening data, on- and off-DNA biophysical measurements, model evaluations in Tables 1-2, and experimental replicate analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds Chemprop and cluster-split evaluations, BCA screening replicate analyses, scaffold statistics and molecular docking outputs.

M1.justification: The retained predictive architectures, objectives and DEL-Compose variants remain unchanged in Section 3.2 and Appendix D. Chemprop is an added comparator; the new splitting and docking procedures extend evaluation and data generation without modifying these predictors.

E1.justification: V2 extends experimental coverage beyond two kinases by adding Bovine Carbonic Anhydrase screening with replicate analysis (Section 4; Figure 7c). Appendix F also reports docking 234k ligand states against six kinase receptor models. The tabulated machine-learning affinity benchmarks still concern MAPK14 and DDR1.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 newly evaluate Chemprop DMPNN against the existing methods, including within the retained random and disynthon comparisons. Counts, Poisson, RF, XGBoost, kNN, DNN, GIN and both DEL-Compose variants remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds a third evaluation split based on UMAP-reduced fingerprints, HDBSCAN clustering and whole-cluster assignment (Section 3.1; Appendix E). Appendix F introduces a specified multi-receptor docking protocol. The original top-1M training selection, random/disynthon protocols, affinity test-set sizes and Spearman metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds cluster-split generalization comparisons and an empirical scaffold-frequency analysis assessing the suitability of scaffold splitting (Appendix E; Figure 9). It also adds held-out affinity distributions, BCA replicate diagnostics and qualitative docking cases (Figures 7-10), substantially extending v1's supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five training runs per splitting strategy, report performance with ± values, and use triplicate DEL measurements. V2 extends these practices to additional results without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test or changed run count for retained experiments.

E6.justification: All 28 pre-existing model/split rows in Tables 1-2 retain their numerical values. V2 adds Chemprop and cluster-split results, including MAPK14 cluster on-DNA correlation 0.713 ± 0.013 for Chemprop and off-DNA correlation 0.766 ± 0.012 for DEL-Compose(S). BCA replicate plots, scaffold statistics, affinity distributions and docking examples add further findings.

T1.justification: No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced. The fluorescence-polarization and binding-curve equations in Appendix A remain mathematically equivalent; the new clustering and docking descriptions specify procedures rather than theoretical results.

C1.justification: V2's abstract adds the claim that KinDEL is the first public DEL dataset containing molecular docking poses and frames its contribution as encompassing both 2D and 3D structures. This expands the central resource claim beyond v1. The conclusion also qualifies the earlier drug-like characterization to many molecules having properties within approved-drug ranges.

C2.justification: V2 interprets cluster splits as offering limited additional difficulty, tentatively associates MAPK14 disynthon degradation with overfitting, and explains objections to scaffold splitting. It adds qualifications about preselection-normalization errors and kinase-only coverage while retaining the principal denoising interpretation and existing applicability limitations.

D1.justification: V2 adds Chemprop hyperparameters, clustering configuration and GPU/runtime information, BCA preparation and assay protocols, and detailed docking software, conformer, receptor and SDF specifications. It newly discloses sequencing depths and the cloning kit and corrects DDR1 gene labels. The existing repository link remains available in the text.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 adds AIRCHECK (Wellnitz et al., 2024), contrasting its masked structures with KinDEL's representation. Additional citations support Chemprop, clustering and docking, and the abstract adds docking-related novelty positioning. The established related-work discussion remains largely intact.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and expands selected dataset, evaluation and discussion passages while retaining the main section order and much existing prose. It updates authorship, adds an Impact Statement and Appendices E-F, and removes the standalone Reproducibility Statement while retaining the repository reference elsewhere.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column conference layout. V2 redraws synthesis/selection graphics, adds a data-schema panel, separates the UMAP and splitting diagrams, and expands the benchmark tables. New appendix displays include BCA replicates, affinity histograms, scaffold structures and docking poses.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens KinDEL's usefulness and reproducibility through a non-kinase screen with replicate diagnostics, documented 3D pose generation, and explicit implementation details. Chemprop comparisons, the additional split and scaffold diagnostics make the evaluation more informative and its design easier to assess. These gains extend beyond presentation, although the unchanged small affinity test sets and absence of BCA/3D predictive benchmarks still limit generalization claims.
